title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation)

(August 30, 1984)

I. Jurisdiction

Jurisdiction is the issue of determining the division of work among people's courts in hearing first-instance civil cases. People's courts at all levels must earnestly implement the various provisions on jurisdiction in the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation) (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), adhere to the principle of "facilitating litigation for the parties and facilitating trial by the court," and properly resolve disputes over jurisdiction.

(1) Where one party is a staff member of the basic people's court accepting the case, or the case is complex, involves a wide scope, and the basic people's court finds it difficult to hear, the case may be submitted to a superior people's court for trial in accordance with Article 34 of the Civil Procedure Law. It may also be subject to designation of jurisdiction by the superior people's court in accordance with Article 33 of the Civil Procedure Law.

(2) The "domicile" referred to in Articles 20 and 21 of the Civil Procedure Law means the place where a party has continuously resided for one year or more.

(3) In divorce proceedings where both parties are active servicemen, the case may generally be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the location of the organ at or above the regimental level of the defendant's military unit.

(4) Where both parties to an action are imprisoned or under reeducation through labor, the case may generally be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the defendant's original place of household registration.

(5) Where both parties to an action have had their urban household registration cancelled due to administrative sanctions imposed by the public security department, the action shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the defendant's domicile. Where the defendant's urban household registration is cancelled, the action shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the plaintiff's place of household registration; if the plaintiff's place of household registration and place of domicile are inconsistent, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the place of domicile.

(6) During the first-instance trial of a civil case, if a new tort occurs between the parties, and it is related to the original case and suitable for consolidated hearing, the cases may be heard together. If the new tort occurs during the second-instance trial, mediation may be conducted together with the original case; if mediation fails, the newly occurred tort shall be handled in a separate case.

(7) Where a people's court discovers that a case it has accepted is not within its jurisdiction, it shall transfer the case to a people's court that has jurisdiction. If the people's court to which the case is transferred considers that the transferred case is not within its jurisdiction, it may report to the common superior people's court for designation of jurisdiction and shall not further transfer the case on its own.

(8) During the trial of a case, if a party's household registration is transferred or his place of domicile changes, the people court hearing the case shall continue the trial and shall not transfer the case.

(9) In a divorce case where the defendant has been hospitalized in a different place for a long period, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court at the defendant's original place of household registration.

II. Participants in Litigation

Protecting the litigation rights of participants in litigation and clarifying their rights and obligations in litigation are conducive to the people's court ascertaining the facts of the case, correctly trying the case, and protecting the lawful rights and interests of the parties.

(10) When examining a complaint, the people's court shall examine whether the parties meet the conditions. During the proceedings, if it is discovered that a party does not meet the conditions, the court shall replace the party in accordance with Article 90 of the Civil Procedure Law. After notification of replacement, if the unqualified plaintiff is unwilling to withdraw from the action, the action shall be dismissed by ruling; if all qualified plaintiffs are unwilling to participate in the action, the trial of the case may be terminated. If the defendant is unqualified and the plaintiff does not agree to the replacement, the action shall be dismissed by ruling.

(11) If a person who must jointly participate in the action has not participated, the people's court shall, in accordance with Article 91 of the Civil Procedure Law, notify him to participate; the parties may also apply to the people's court to add the person. The people's court shall examine the application submitted by a party; if the application is groundless, it may be dismissed by ruling; if the application is justified, the court shall promptly notify the added party in writing to participate in the action.

(12) If during the proceedings the second-instance people's court discovers the need to replace or add a party, and after replacement or addition, no agreement can be reached between the parties through mediation, the case shall be remanded for retrial.

(13) When adding an original plaintiff to a joint action, the people's court shall notify the other parties. If the added plaintiff has clearly indicated waiver of substantive rights, he may not be added; if he is neither willing to participate in the action nor waives substantive rights, he shall still be added as a plaintiff, and even if he does not appear in court, it shall not affect the people's court's trial and lawful judgment of the case.

(14) The legal representative of an organ, organization, enterprise, or institution shall be its principal responsible person in charge of administrative work. If there is no such principal responsible person, the deputy may serve as the legal representative. The legal representative has the right to appoint an agent ad litem in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law.

(15) During the proceedings, if an organ, organization, enterprise, or institution that is a party undergoes reorganization or a change in its principal responsible person, a certificate of identity of the new legal representative shall be submitted to the people's court, and the proceedings shall continue. The litigation activities already conducted shall be binding on the legal representative who continues to participate.

(16) In accordance with Article 48 of the Civil Procedure Law, a third party without independent claim may apply to participate in the action, and the people's court shall also notify him to participate. If the people's court confirms in its judgment that such a third party assumes obligations, he has the right to appeal; if a mediation agreement imposes obligations on him, his consent shall be sought.

(17) In a divorce case where a party lacks capacity, the parents, adult children, or siblings who live with and have a support relationship with the party may act as legal representatives to participate in the action; if there are no such relatives, or if such relatives have genuine difficulties in acting as representatives, the agency, organization, enterprise, or institution to which the party belongs may act as legal representative.

(18) In a divorce action, if the legal representative is unwilling to appear in court, the people's court shall patiently explain and persuade him to appear; if he still does not appear, the court may obtain his opinion on the spot and, after ascertaining the facts, render a judgment according to law.

(19) When a party appoints an agent ad litem, he shall submit a power of attorney to the people's court. The power of attorney must be examined and approved by the people's court. To revoke the appointment, a written report shall be submitted to the people's court.

(20) When a party or agent ad litem requests to review the trial transcripts and evidence materials of the case in accordance with Articles 45 and 53 of the Civil Procedure Law, such review must be conducted within the people's court. The materials that have been permitted for review may be excerpted, but shall not be reproduced without authorization.

Records of the collegial panel's deliberations, records of the adjudication committee's discussions, the original legal documents, and materials concerning the people's court's study and discussion of the case shall not be made available for review by the parties or agents ad litem.

(21) During the proceedings, if one party dies and it is necessary to await the heir to participate in the action, the people's court shall promptly notify the heir to assume the action as a party, and shall not continue to list the deceased as a party.

III. Mediation

The people's court, when trying civil cases, shall focus on mediation. Mediation shall adhere to the principles of voluntariness and legality, and shall rely on the party's work unit, grassroots organizations, and the party's relatives and friends to do more ideological work and, as far as possible, help solve certain practical problems. It is necessary to prevent forcing parties to accept mediation and to avoid prolonged mediation without resolution.

(22) For divorce cases where mediation results in reconciliation, and for compensation and debt cases where the amount in dispute is small and the mediation agreement can be fully performed immediately, the basic people's court generally may not prepare a mediation document. The clerk shall record the mediation agreement in the trial transcript, and once signed or sealed by both parties, the trial personnel, and the clerk, it shall have legal effect.

(23) The mediation document shall be directly served on the party himself. If one party refuses to sign for receipt, it shall be deemed that mediation has failed, the original mediation document shall have no effect, and the people's court shall promptly notify the other party and continue the trial.

(24) In a divorce case involving a person without capacity, issues such as divorce, property, and child support may be negotiated between the legal representative or appointed agent ad litem and the other party. If an agreement is reached, the case shall generally be concluded by judgment.

(25) When a people's court mediates a case, if a party cannot appear in court, the party may, with special authorization, have his appointed agent ad litem attend and negotiate. However, for divorce cases, the party must submit a written opinion to the court in accordance with Article 54 of the Civil Procedure Law.

(26) If a case concluded by mediation is later found to be erroneous, it shall be handled in accordance with the provisions on trial supervision procedures.

IV. Evidence

Evidence is the basis for ascertaining and determining the truth of a case. Having sufficient and conclusive evidence is the foundation for correctly handling a case. Collecting and investigating evidence comprehensively and objectively, carefully examining evidence, and accurately assessing evidence are of particular importance for improving the quality of case handling.

(27) Collection and investigation of evidence shall be presided over by the trial personnel and carried out by two or more persons jointly. The investigation materials shall state the investigator, the person investigated, the recorder, and the time and place of the investigation, and shall be signed or sealed by the investigator, the person investigated, and the recorder.

(28) When collecting and investigating evidence, the people's court shall go deep among the masses, rely on relevant organizations, and carefully ascertain the time, place, cause, process, and result of the dispute, without being limited by the scope of evidence provided by the parties.

(29) Certified copies of materials excerpted from relevant units shall state the name and source of the excerpted materials and shall be sealed by the relevant unit.

(30) The main evidence used as the basis for deciding the case shall be presented in court or read out, and both parties shall be allowed to debate and challenge the evidence.

V. Compulsory Measures

Taking compulsory measures against acts that obstruct civil litigation is a compulsory means to remove obstacles and ensure the normal conduct of litigation activities. The people's court may, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, take corresponding compulsory measures against a participant in the proceedings or any other person who intentionally obstructs civil litigation during the proceedings, constituting any of the acts referred to in Article 77 of the Civil Procedure Law. However, such measures must be taken with caution, the work must be done effectively, and the relevant procedures must be strictly followed.

(31) If a defendant who must appear in court, after being lawfully summoned twice by subpoena, refuses to appear without justifiable reasons, the court may issue a warrant for compulsory appearance. The compulsory appearance must be effected by a warrant for compulsory appearance, which shall be directly served on the person to be compelled, and he shall be informed of the consequences of refusing to appear. If, after criticism and education, he still refuses to appear, he may be compelled to appear.

(32) A defendant who must appear in court generally refers to a defendant who has an obligation to pay alimony, support, or maintenance, or a defendant whose failure to appear would make it impossible to ascertain the facts of the case.

If the legal representative of a minor who has caused damage to the state, collective, or another person is a person who must appear in court, the warrant for compulsory appearance may also be applied.

(33) When handling a case on circuit or at a local court session and it is necessary to take the compulsory measure of detention, oral or written instructions shall be sought from the president for approval before implementation. If urgent detention measures are necessary due to disturbances in court, physical assault, etc., and there is no time to seek instructions from the president, the measures may be taken first, and the president shall be immediately reported to for retroactive approval. If the president considers that the measures taken are improper, the original decision shall be revoked and the compulsory measures shall be lifted.

(34) After the decision to detain is announced, efforts to persuade and educate the detained person shall still be made. If the detained person admits his mistake and repents on the spot, the matter may be reported to the president for a decision to temporarily postpone or lift the detention; if during the period of detention, he admits his mistake and repents after education, the detention may be lifted early.

(35) Fines may be applied to citizens and to the directly responsible personnel of organs and organizations.

Fines may be imposed together with detention, or separately.

VI. Filing and Acceptance of Cases

After receiving a complaint from a party, the people's court shall examine it and decide within the statutory period whether to accept the case. Doing a good job in examining complaints and accepting cases is very important for protecting the parties' litigation rights, preventing frivolous lawsuits, and ensuring the correct handling of cases.

(36) After receiving the plaintiff's complaint, if the people's court, after careful examination, considers that the conditions for acceptance under the Civil Procedure Law are not met, it shall notify the plaintiff of the non-acceptance and state the reasons. If the plaintiff persists in filing the case, the case may be docketed and accepted. If further investigation reveals that the complaint indeed does not meet the acceptance conditions, the action shall be dismissed by written ruling.

(37) If a mediation organization or relevant grassroots organization requests the people's court to handle a civil dispute that cannot be settled through mediation, the parties themselves shall file a complaint directly with the people's court.

(38) The time limit for filing a case as provided in Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law shall be calculated from the day following the day on which the people's court receives the complaint. If the complaint is returned for supplementation of deficiencies, the time limit shall be calculated from the day following the day on which the supplemented complaint is submitted to the court. For cases transferred from a superior people's court to a lower people's court, or from a basic people's court to a relevant people's court for acceptance, the time limit shall be calculated from the day following the day on which the people's court or people's tribunal hearing the case receives the complaint.

(39) If the complaint contains abusive or personally attacking language and serving a copy of the complaint might cause new disputes or aggravate conflicts, making it unfavorable for the resolution of the case, the people's court shall persuade the party to modify the complaint based on facts. If the party insists on not making changes, the court may briefly notify the other party of the content of the complaint orally or in writing. If the defendant insists on seeing the complaint, a copy of the complaint may also be served.

(40) The decision to notify non-acceptance after examining a plaintiff's complaint shall be made by the trial judge or the division chief; after a case is docketed, the decision on which procedure to apply for trial shall be made by the trial judge; a ruling to dismiss the action shall be made by the president or by the division chief authorized by the president.

(41) For a divorce case where the parties have reconciled through mediation, the plaintiff has voluntarily withdrawn the complaint, or the case has been treated as withdrawn, if the plaintiff files another complaint within six months without new circumstances or new reasons, the court shall not accept the case by analogy with Article 84, item (5) of the Civil Procedure Law.

(42) If an act of infringing upon personal rights or damaging public or private property violates criminal law and constitutes a crime, it shall not be handled as a civil case. A dispute over compensation arising from a criminal act of the defendant shall be handled as a criminal supplementary civil action in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law. If it is difficult to determine at the time whether a criminal law violation has occurred, the case shall be docketed based on the plaintiff's claim.

(43) Disputes over housing left over from various political movements that involve implementing policies, disputes arising from the division of responsibility fields or planning of residential land in rural areas, disputes over illegal construction, disputes over the validity of divorce registration, and other disputes that should be handled by administrative departments according to law shall be resolved by informing the plaintiff to apply to the relevant department for resolution.

VII. Ordinary Procedure

Ordinary procedure is the basic procedure in trial procedures. When trying major or complex first-instance civil cases, the people's court shall apply ordinary procedure and form a collegial panel to conduct the trial. Proper application of ordinary procedure is conducive to ascertaining the facts of the case and correctly applying the law, to conducting legal propaganda, and to the smooth enforcement of judgments.

(44) When trying a first-instance civil case, whether by mediation or judgment, whether applying summary or ordinary procedure, and whether trying inside the court or on circuit at the local level, the people's court shall open a court session to inform the parties of their litigation rights and obligations, hear their statements, present necessary evidence, and allow both parties to debate.

(45) If the legal representative of a party without litigation capacity, after being lawfully summoned twice, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons and has not appointed an agent ad litem, and if the party is the plaintiff, the case may be treated as withdrawn by analogy with Article 112 of the Civil Procedure Law; if the party is the defendant, a default judgment may be rendered by analogy with Article 113 of the Civil Procedure Law.

(46) If, after the plaintiff applies for withdrawal and the people's court rules not to permit the withdrawal, the plaintiff refuses to appear in court, a default judgment may be rendered by analogy with the principle of Article 112 of the Civil Procedure Law.

(47) When the cause for the suspension of proceedings is eliminated and the proceedings are resumed, there is no need to revoke the original ruling. From the time the people's court notifies or permits the parties to continue the proceedings, the ruling to suspend the proceedings loses effect.

(48) If, after a first-instance case has been concluded and publicly announced or a judgment has been served, the original trial court discovers an error during the appeal period, the matter shall, after the appeal period expires, be submitted by the president to the adjudication committee for discussion. If it is considered that there is indeed an error, a retrial shall be conducted in accordance with the trial supervision procedure. If a party files an appeal, the case shall be tried according to the appeal procedure, and the original trial people's court may submit an opinion stating that the original judgment is erroneous to the appellate people's court.

(49) If a legal document that has taken legal effect contains errors in writing, miscalculation, omission of the decision on litigation costs, or other mistakes, the people's court that made the legal document may correct them by ruling. If a claim made during the trial is omitted from the judgment, or if the holding of the judgment is unclear and cannot be enforced, the people's court that made the judgment may render a supplementary judgment. A supplementary judgment made by a first-instance people's court may be appealed by a party who is dissatisfied; a supplementary judgment made by a second-instance people's court is a final judgment.

VIII. Summary Procedure

The provisions on summary procedure reflect the characteristics of the Civil Procedure Law that facilitate litigation for the parties and facilitate the trial work of the people's court. Proper application of summary procedure is conducive to concluding cases in a timely manner. Summary procedure applies only to simple civil cases tried by basic people's courts and the people's tribunals dispatched by them, and the scope of application of summary procedure shall not be expanded arbitrarily.

(50) The following types of cases may apply summary procedure:

1. Divorce cases where the marriage period is short and the dispute over property is not significant, or where one party suffered from a disease that prevents marriage according to law before marriage.

2. Cases concerning alimony, support, or maintenance where the rights and obligations are clear and the dispute is only over the time and amount of payment.

3. Cases of confirming or changing an adoption or foster relationship where the dispute between the parties is not significant.

4. Debt cases where the loan relationship is clear, the evidence is sufficient, and the amount is not large.

5. Inheritance cases where the scope of the estate and heirs is clear and the amount of the estate in dispute is not large.

6. Damage compensation cases where the facts are clear, the liability is definite, and the amount of compensation is not large.

7. Other cases where the facts are clear, the circumstances are simple, right and wrong are clear, the focus of the dispute is clear, and the amount in dispute is not large.

(51) When trying a case using summary procedure, the content of the complaint shall be notified to the defendant orally or in writing. The case shall be tried by a single judge with a clerk to keep the record; the judge shall not both try the case and keep the record. If the case is concluded by judgment, a public pronouncement of the judgment shall be made in accordance with Article 115 of the Civil Procedure Law.

(52) A people's tribunal is a dispatched agency and component part of a basic people's court. In accordance with Articles 101, 120, and 122 of the Civil Procedure Law, judgments, mediation documents, and rulings made by a people's tribunal must bear the seal of the people's court, and the seal of the people's tribunal shall not be used to replace the seal of the basic people's court.

IX. Special Procedure

Special procedure is the procedure for trying several types of special cases that do not involve civil rights and interests disputes. Cases that must be tried under special procedure shall strictly comply with the conditions and procedures provided in the Civil Procedure Law.

(53) A declaration of death of a missing person requires an application from the applicant, accompanied by a written certificate from the public security organ certifying the person's disappearance; otherwise, the case shall not be accepted.

If one party is missing and the other party only seeks a divorce without applying for a declaration of death, the special procedure for declaring a missing person dead shall not apply. If the absent person has had no contact with the family for two consecutive years or more, and after extensive search, his whereabouts cannot be ascertained, and the other party insists on a divorce, the litigation documents may be served by public announcement, and a judgment may be rendered according to law after the expiration of the announcement period. After the judgment is served by public announcement, it shall take legal effect upon the expiration of the appeal period.

(54) If a party is a mental patient, as long as he has been diagnosed by a relevant hospital as suffering from a mental illness, there is no need to first apply special procedure to declare him incapacitated.

X. Second Instance and Trial Supervision

[No content under this heading in the provided text.]

(55) Legal representatives of persons lacking capacity to act may file appeals and petitions for retrial on their behalf.

(56) Cases remanded for retrial or retried shall, in accordance with Article 36 of the Civil Procedure Law, be tried by a newly formed collegial panel, and summary procedure with a single judge shall not apply. Members of the original collegial panel or the original sole judge may not participate in the newly formed collegial panel.

(57) Judgments in appellate cases, retrial cases, and cases transferred for trial shall be publicly pronounced in all cases. The court that rendered the judgment may pronounce it itself, or may entrust the original trial court to pronounce it on its behalf.

(58) Where the Supreme People's Court finds that a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement of a local people's court at any level, or a higher people's court finds that such a decision of a lower people's court, or a people's court finds that such a decision of its own, is indeed erroneous and requires a transfer for trial, an order to the lower court to retry, or a retrial by itself, the court shall issue an order for transfer, order for retrial, or order for its own retrial. Such order may include a provision for suspension of enforcement.

(59) When a case is decided to be retried or transferred for trial under the trial supervision procedure, the original judgment need not be revoked first. The court conducting the retrial or transfer shall determine whether to revoke it in the new judgment. If a mediation agreement is reached, the original judgment shall be deemed revoked upon service of the mediation document.

(60) Where a case adjudicated or mediated by a higher people's court requires retrial, it shall be retried by that higher people's court itself and shall not be ordered to be retried by a lower people's court.

(61) Where one or some of the necessary joint litigants file an appeal alone, and the appeal gives rise to a severable claim, the other parties on the same side need not be listed in the legal documents. If the claim is not severable, all other parties shall be listed as appellees.

(62) Where both parties are dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance and both file appeals, both may be listed as appellants.

XI. Issues of Enforcement

Enforcement is the final stage of civil proceedings and is an important system for safeguarding the dignity of the law and protecting the lawful rights and interests of the parties. It is necessary to correctly understand and apply enforcement procedures, distinguish the boundary between voluntary performance and compulsory enforcement, clarify the objects of enforcement, observe the time limits for applying for enforcement, and correctly take compulsory enforcement measures.

(63) The subject matter of compulsory enforcement can only be property or acts. Where a party refuses to perform a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement, legal education and persuasion shall first be conducted. If education is ineffective, compulsory enforcement shall be carried out. If, during compulsory enforcement, a party or a third party intentionally obstructs civil proceedings, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 77 of the Civil Procedure Law. If the circumstances are serious and constitute a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with Article 157 of the Criminal Law.

(64) Where a bailiff, during enforcement of a judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement of his own court, finds a definite error, he shall submit a written opinion to the president for review and handling. Where, during enforcement of a judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement that has been entrusted for enforcement by a higher people's court or a court in another locality, a definite error is found, a written opinion may be submitted. Upon approval by the president, the matter shall be referred by letter to the higher people's court or the court in the other locality for review and handling. Pending such review, enforcement shall be temporarily suspended.

(65) Where a party applies for enforcement of an award of an arbitral body in accordance with Article 167 of the Civil Procedure Law, and the people's court finds a definite error, upon approval by the president, it may notify the arbitral body to reconsider and suspend enforcement.

(66) When an administrative authority's decision is applied to a people's court for compulsory enforcement in accordance with law, it must submit an application for enforcement, the legal document on which enforcement is based, and any other necessary materials. If the people's court finds a definite error in the decision, it may return it to the relevant authority for reconsideration.

(67) Where, during enforcement, it is discovered that property subject to seizure or distraint has been damaged, sold, transferred, or lost, besides handling the matter in accordance with Article 77 of the Civil Procedure Law, the bailiff shall order the judgment debtor to surrender the property or compensate for the loss. If the judgment debtor refuses to surrender or compensate, enforcement shall be ordered by ruling.

(68) Where a specific item is to be enforced, the original item shall be enforced. If the original item no longer exists, compensation may be made at its appraised value.

(69) Where, during enforcement, the parties dispute the subject matter of enforcement as determined in the original legal document, ideological work shall be done to encourage voluntary performance. If the parties voluntarily reach a settlement agreement, the agreement shall be recorded in the case file, signed or sealed by both parties, and enforcement shall be terminated.

XII. Issues of Handling Cases Involving Hong Kong and Macau Compatriots

Cases involving Hong Kong and Macau compatriots are not foreign-related cases. In view of the special status of the Hong Kong and Macau regions, such cases may be handled by reference to Part Five of the Civil Procedure Law and other relevant provisions.

(70) Cases involving Hong Kong and Macau compatriots shall generally be tried by a basic people's court as the court of first instance. Major or complex cases shall be tried by an intermediate people's court as the court of first instance.

(71) Where a couple originally married in mainland China and later settled in Hong Kong or Macau, and both parties return to mainland China to file a divorce lawsuit in a people's court for special reasons, the case may be accepted by the people's court at the place of original marriage registration, the place where the marriage was contracted, or the place of the defendant's original household registration.

(72) Powers of attorney and written opinions on divorce cases sent by Hong Kong or Macau compatriots to mainland China shall be handled in accordance with the Notice of the Ministry of Justice of April 29, 1981 (No. (81) Si Fa Gong Zi 129) on the Issuance of Certificates for Hong Kong and Macau Compatriots Returning to the Mainland to Apply for Notarization and the Supplementary Notice of February 20, 1982 (No. (82) Si Fa Gong Zi 39) on the Issuance of Certificates for Hong Kong and Macau Compatriots Returning to the Mainland to Apply for Notarization.

(73) Service of litigation documents by a people's court on a party residing in Hong Kong or Macau may be effected by mail or through the party's litigation representative. If such methods are not feasible, service by publication may be used. Service shall be deemed to have been made upon the expiration of three months from the date of publication.

(74) If a party from Hong Kong or Macau who is required to appear in court or to continue participating in litigation activities requests to leave the country, he shall provide a bond to the people's court.

XIII. Issues of Foreign-Related Litigation Procedure

When a people's court hears a civil case where one or both parties are foreigners, stateless persons, foreign enterprises, or organizations, it shall apply the special provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on foreign-related civil procedure, adhering to the principles of sovereignty, reciprocity, and equality of litigation rights and obligations of the parties.

When a people's court hears a civil case where the property in dispute is located abroad, or where the legal facts giving rise to, changing, or extinguishing the civil legal relationship occur abroad, it may handle the case by reference to Part Five of the Civil Procedure Law and other relevant provisions.

(75) Where a civil dispute involves one or both parties being foreigners, stateless persons, foreign enterprises, or organizations, and the party files a lawsuit with a people's court that has jurisdiction, the court shall accept and docket the case.

The exclusive jurisdiction provided for in Article 30 of the Civil Procedure Law cannot be altered by agreement of the parties.

(76) Where overseas Chinese who married in China and later settled abroad have their divorce petition rejected by the court of the country of residence on the ground that the divorce action must be filed in the court of the place of marriage or the court of the country of nationality, and both parties return to China and request a people's court to handle the matter, the case may be accepted by the people's court at the place of original marriage registration or the place of the defendant's original household registration.

(77) Where overseas Chinese married and settled abroad, their divorce cases shall in principle not be accepted by a people's court. If the country of residence refuses to accept the case on the ground of the parties' nationality, and both parties return to China and request a people's court to handle the matter, the case may be accepted by the people's court at the place of the defendant's original household registration.

(78) Where one Chinese citizen resides abroad (including those who have gone abroad for family visits, investigations, or studies) and the other resides in China, no matter which party files the divorce action, the lawsuit shall be filed in the people's court at the place of household registration or residence of the party in China. If the party abroad files a divorce action in a court of the country of residence, and the party in China also files a divorce action in a people's court, the people's court that accepts the case may accept it in accordance with Article 21, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law.

(79) Where a party not residing in China is unable to appear in court due to filing or defending a divorce action in a people's court, he must submit a written opinion to the people's court. If such written opinion is sent to the people's court from abroad, for a foreigner, it must be notarized by a notary public of the country of residence and certified by the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country; for an overseas Chinese, it must be certified by the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country, or, if there is no such embassy or consulate, by a patriotic overseas Chinese organization.

(80) A foreign court's divorce judgment involving a Chinese citizen may be recognized as binding on both parties if it does not violate the basic spirit of China's marriage law and the parties have no objection. If such judgment is to be enforced in China, the foreign court must entrust a Chinese people's court with enforcement in accordance with Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law.

(81) Where a party residing abroad applies for preservation of property located in China in a lawsuit, he must provide a bond.

(82) An outline of questions for a people's court to investigate a Chinese citizen residing abroad shall, after review by a higher people's court, be forwarded to the Consular Department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for transmission to the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country for conducting the inquiry.
